facts.text: Brookdale Lodge, built in 1890, became a glamorous resort hosting stars like Marilyn Monroe, James Dean, and President Herbert Hoover during its mid‑20th‑century heyday.
The town’s name changed to Brookdale in 1903 when the post office opened, coinciding with the arrival of the Southern Pacific Railroad’s narrow‑gauge line.
Brookdale once thrived as a logging camp in the late 1800s, leaving behind remnants of old mills that visitors can still see today.
In the 1920s and 1930s, Brookdale’s resort era rivaled Clear Creek Villa, which hosted dances, orchestras, and celebrities amid Prohibition‑era rumors of bootlegging.
A 1929 lawsuit over the “Brookdale” name reached the California Supreme Court but was dismissed in 1932, preserving the town’s identity.
The historic Brookdale Lodge earned a plaque from the Ancient and Honorable Order of E Clampus Vitus in 2021, marking its enduring cultural heritage.
